steps.description:
Create a program that asks the user to enter his or her feeling. Using if-else statement, perform the following: 1. display "You are happy!" if the input is "happy" 2. display "Tell me when you are happy" if the input is not "happy"

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input bored

mad

happy

hApPy

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the 4 examples below:

Example 1 How do you feel? bored Tell me when you are happy

Example 2 How do you feel? mad Tell me when you are happy

Example 3 How do you feel? happy You are happy!

Example 4 How do you feel? hApPy Tell me when you are happy

Create a program that asks the user to enter his or her feeling. Using if-else statement, perform the following: 1. Display "You are happy!" if the input is "happy", regardless of whether the letters are small or capital letters. 2. Display "Tell me when you are happy" if the input is not "happy"

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input bored

mad

happy

hApPy

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 How do you feel? bored Tell me when you are happy

Example 2 How do you feel? mad Tell me when you are happy

Example 3 How do you feel? happy You are happy!

Example 4 How do you feel? hApPy You are happy!

Create a program that asks the user to enter an integer. Using if-else statement, display "not zero" if the integer is not equal to 0. Otherwise, display "zero".

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 0

1

-1

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input integer: 0 zero

Example 2 Input integer: 1 not zero

Example 3 Input integer: -1 not zero

Create a program that asks the user to enter a float. Using if-else statement, display "negative" if the float is less than 0. Otherwise, display "not negative".

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 0

0.001

-0.001

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input float: 0 not negative

Example 2 Input float: 0.001 not negative

Example 3 Input float: -0.001 negative

Create a program that asks the user to enter 2 floats. Using if-else statement, display "sum within 10" if the sum of the floats is less than or equal to 10. Otherwise, display "sum over 10".

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 5 4.5

3 7

5.1 4.99

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input 2 floats: 5 4.5 sum within 10

Example 2 Input 2 floats: 3 7 sum within 10

Example 3 Input 2 floats: 5.1 4.99 sum over 10

Create a program that asks the user to enter 2 integers in a row. Using if-else statement, display "ascending" if the second integer is more than the first integer. Otherwise, display "not ascending".

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input 1 9

-2 -1

9 9

10 9

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input 2 integers: 1 9 ascending

Example 2 Input 2 integers: -2 -1 ascending

Example 3 Input 2 integers: 9 9 not ascending

Example 4 Input 2 integers: 10 9 not ascending

Create a program that asks the user to enter 4 integers in a row and calculate their average. Using if-else statement, display the average if it is more than or equal to 10. Otherwise, display "too low".

Follow the test output display format.

Note that when you divide integers, the result becomes a float.

Test Input 6 10 12 11

0 5 15 20

30 -10 0 22

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input 4 integers: 6 10 12 11 too low

Example 2 Input 4 integers: 0 5 15 20 10.0

Example 3 Input 4 integers: 30 -10 0 22 10.5
